text: This will be my third visit to you. "Every matter must be established by the testimony of two or three witnesses."
I already warned you when I was with you the second time, and I warn you again now while absent, to those who sinned before and to all the rest: if I come again, I will not spare anyone,
since you are demanding proof that Christ speaks through me. He is not weak in dealing with you; he is powerful among you.
For he was crucified in weakness, yet he lives by the power of God. And we too are weak in him, yet in dealing with you we will live with him by the power of God.
Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Or do you not realize about yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you — unless, of course, you fail the test?

versions.text: Examine yourselves to see whether you are in the faith; test yourselves. Do you not realize that Jesus Christ is in you? — unless, of course, you fail the test.
versions.explanation: The disjunctive ἢ ("or") and the reflexive ἑαυτοὺς ("about yourselves") are unrepresented, and the current punctuation (question mark followed by a dash) is awkward for oral reading.

text: And I hope you will come to see that we ourselves have not failed the test.

versions.text: And I trust you will discover that we have not failed the test.
versions.explanation: ἐλπίζω is better rendered "hope" than "trust"; "trust" shifts the nuance toward confidence in the readers rather than Paul's expectation. The emphatic ἡμεῖς ("we ourselves") also picks up the contrast with the preceding verse.

text: We pray to God that you may do nothing wrong — not so that we may appear approved, but so that you may do what is right, even if we should seem to have failed.
For we can do nothing against the truth, but only for the truth.
For we rejoice whenever we are weak and you are strong; and this too is what we pray for: your full restoration.

versions.text: We rejoice whenever we are weak and you are strong; and this is what we pray for: your restoration.
versions.explanation: The connective γὰρ links this verse to the preceding argument and is currently dropped; the καὶ in τοῦτο καὶ εὐχόμεθα ("this too we pray") is likewise unrepresented.

text: This is why I write these things while absent, so that when I come I need not deal harshly in using the authority the Lord gave me — authority for building up, not for tearing down.
Finally, brothers and sisters, rejoice. Be restored, be encouraged, be of one mind, live in peace; and the God of love and peace will be with you.
Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints send you greetings.
The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.
